title: Tools to Assess Vulnerabilities
bigQuestion: How do organisations find their weaknesses before attackers do?

sections.heading: Vulnerability assessment
sections.text: Finding, listing and ranking the weaknesses in a system, network or app, before an attacker can use them. Like a car service that finds faults before the car breaks down.
points: Open ports that aren't needed
Missing updates and security patches
Weak or wrong settings (configuration)
Risky user behaviour

head: Vulnerability assessment
Penetration testing
rows: An ethical hacker tries to break in, with permission
Does NOT try to break in

sections.heading: A2.4.1 Port scanner
sections.text: Sends a request to each numbered port and records the reply.
points: Open: accepts the connection, a service is listening
Closed: replies, but nothing is listening
Filtered: no reply, a firewall is blocking it
An open port is only a problem if it isn't needed or isn't protected

sections.heading: A2.4.2 Network mapper / system discovery
sections.text: Draws a map of every device: routers, switches, firewalls, access points, PCs, servers.
points: Spots rogue devices, e.g. an unknown wireless access point
Keeps the list of devices to patch up to date
System discovery builds a detailed list: IP address, operating system, protocols

sections.heading: A2.4.3 Registry checker
sections.text: The Windows registry is a database of settings (not files), stored as keys and values.
points: Attackers change keys to run malware at start-up or switch off antivirus/firewall
The checker finds unauthorised changes so they can be undone

sections.heading: A2.4.4 Website vulnerability scanner
sections.text: Sends test requests to a site and checks for OWASP Top 10 risks, then produces a report.
points: SQL injection: database commands typed into a form
XSS: a harmful script runs in visitors' browsers
Weak TLS/SSL: old encryption, data could be intercepted
Exposed admin page: /admin reachable with no protection

sections.heading: A2.4.5 Detection & management software
points: Scan devices against a database of known vulnerabilities
Score each one with CVSS (0 to 10)
Prioritise the most dangerous and easiest to exploit
Track each fix until it is done and produce reports

sections.heading: A2.4.6 Assessing user vulnerabilities
sections.text: People are often the weakest link.
points: Device checks: updates and patches installed?
Phishing simulation: who clicks a fake email?
Physical social engineering: e.g. following staff through a door
Password audits & observation: weak passwords, sticky notes, unlocked screens

sections.heading: Limitations of automated tools
points: Zero-day flaws: brand new, not in the database yet, so missed
False positive: flags a problem that isn't there, wasting time
False negative: misses a real problem, giving a false sense of security
Lacks context: can't judge how important a system is to the business

keyIdea: No single tool is enough. Each tool only covers one area (ports, devices, settings, websites, people). Attackers use whichever weakness is easiest, so organisations need a combination of tools, regular scanning and human judgement.
flashcards: Finding, listing and ranking (prioritising) the weaknesses in a system, network or app, before an attacker can use them.

Replies, but nothing is listening right now. Could become open later, so keep scanning.
No reply at all: a firewall is blocking it.
Remote Desktop. High risk if open to the internet: a password-guessing target.
FTP (file transfer). Risky because data is not encrypted.
Draws a map of every device on a network and spots rogue or unexpected devices.
Builds a detailed list of connected devices with their IP address, operating system and protocols.

Scans the registry for unauthorised or suspicious changes so they can be undone.

A list of the most serious web application security risks.
Database commands typed into a form or search box let an attacker read or change records.
A harmful script is saved on a page and runs in the browser of anyone who views it.

A severity score from 0 to 10. Higher = more serious, so fix it first.

quiz.q: Which port number is normally used for HTTP web traffic?
quiz.e: Port 80 is HTTP. 443 is HTTPS, 21 is FTP and 3389 is Remote Desktop.

quiz.q: What is the difference between a threat and a vulnerability?
o: A threat is a weakness; a vulnerability is an attacker
A vulnerability is a weakness; a threat is something that could exploit it
A threat only applies to websites
quiz.e: A vulnerability is the weakness (e.g. an open port). A threat is what could take advantage of it (e.g. a hacker or malware).

quiz.q: A company pays an ethical hacker to try to break into its web server to see how much data they can reach. What is this?
quiz.e: Penetration testing actively tries to break in, with permission. A vulnerability assessment only finds and lists weaknesses.

quiz.q: A port scanner sends a request to port 25 and gets no response at all. Which state is the port in?
quiz.e: No reply means a firewall is blocking it: filtered. A closed port still replies.

quiz.q: True or false: "Every open port is a vulnerability."
quiz.e: False. An open port is only a problem if it isn't needed or isn't protected.

quiz.q: A port replies, but nothing is listening. Why keep an eye on it?
o: It could become open later, e.g. when new software is installed
Closed ports slow the network down
It means the firewall has failed
quiz.e: A closed port can become open when new software is installed, so scan regularly.

quiz.q: Which state would you WANT an unused port to show to someone on the internet?
quiz.e: Filtered: the attacker gets no reply and learns nothing about the device.

quiz.q: A scanner opens /admin on a website with no password needed. Which vulnerability is this?
quiz.e: An exposed admin page: the control panel can be reached by anyone with no protection.

quiz.q: Which is more serious: a CVSS score of 9.8 or 4.3?
quiz.e: CVSS runs from 0 to 10. Higher means more serious.

quiz.q: What does the Windows registry store?
o: Settings for Windows, users, software and security
quiz.e: The registry stores settings as keys and values, not files.

quiz.q: Which is usually worse: a false positive or a false negative?
quiz.e: A false negative: a real vulnerability is missed, so the organisation thinks it is safe when it is not.

quiz.q: Odd one out: port scanner, network mapper, phishing simulation, registry checker.
quiz.e: Phishing simulation tests people. The other three test technology.

quiz.q: Why can automated software miss a brand-new flaw in a booking system?
o: It is a zero-day: not yet in the tool's database
quiz.e: Zero-day flaws are brand new, so they are not in the database the tool checks against.

quiz.q: Oakfield Surgery: A Port 3389 open (9.8), B old TLS (7.4), C 4-character passwords (6.5), D minor browser update (4.3). Most urgent first?
quiz.e: Order by CVSS: A, B, C, D. A is open to the whole internet and gives remote control of a machine holding patient data.

apply.title: Pick the tool
apply.intro: Exam questions often give you a scenario and ask which tool to use. Pick the best one for each job.

items.task: Check that no one has plugged an unknown device into the network.
items.e: A network mapper shows every device, including rogue ones.

items.task: Test the school website for SQL injection.
items.e: SQL injection is an OWASP Top 10 risk, tested by website vulnerability scanners.

items.task: Check whether staff would fall for a fake email.
items.e: A phishing simulation assesses user vulnerabilities.

items.task: See which ports on a server can be reached from the internet.
items.e: A port scanner reports each port as open, closed or filtered.

items.task: Check a PC for unauthorised changes to its start-up settings.
items.e: Start-up settings live in the Windows registry.

items.task: Score, prioritise and track fixes over time.
items.e: Detection & management software scans, scores, prioritises and tracks.

items.task: Get a list of every device's IP address and operating system.
items.e: System discovery builds a detailed device list.

items.task: Find out if the online shop uses an old encryption protocol.
items.e: Weak TLS/SSL is checked by a website vulnerability scanner.

items.task: Check whether staff leave passwords on sticky notes.
items.e: Password audits and observation assess user vulnerabilities.

items.task: Find out whether malware has switched off the antivirus on reception PCs.
items.e: Malware disables antivirus by changing registry keys.

items.task: Make sure no fix is forgotten after a long list of problems is found.
items.e: Tracking fixes until done is the job of management software.

items.task: Check whether Remote Desktop is exposed on a server.
items.e: Remote Desktop uses port 3389; a port scanner shows if it is open.

exam.sc: Riverside Leisure runs three leisure centres. Members book classes and pay online through its website. Reception staff use Windows PCs connected to the company network.
exam.q: 1. State the three possible states of a port found by a port scanner.
pts: Open
Closed
Filtered

exam.sc: Riverside Leisure runs three leisure centres. Members book classes and pay online through its website. Reception staff use Windows PCs connected to the company network.
exam.q: 2. Explain one reason why Riverside Leisure should use a registry checker on its reception PCs.
pts: Point: malware/an attacker could change registry settings on the reception PCs, e.g. run malware at start-up or switch off antivirus
Linked reason: the checker detects these unauthorised changes so they can be undone, protecting members' payment data
exam.tip: Use the scenario (reception PCs, members' payments) and link with "…so…".

exam.sc: Riverside Leisure runs three leisure centres. Members book classes and pay online through its website. Reception staff use Windows PCs connected to the company network.
exam.q: 3. Describe how Riverside Leisure could assess whether its reception staff are a security vulnerability.
pts: Phishing simulation: send a fake email and record who clicks or enters details
Password audit / observation: weak passwords, sticky notes, unlocked screens
Physical social engineering: a trusted third party tries to get into staff-only areas
Device checks: latest updates and patches installed
exam.tip: Any 3 points. Finish by saying the results target training.

exam.q:
4. A port scanner has tested three ports. State the state of each.
(i) Port 23 sends back a refusal, nothing is listening.
(ii) Port 445 gives no reply, a firewall drops the request.
(iii) Port 22 accepts the connection and starts an SSH session.
pts: (i) Closed
(ii) Filtered
(iii) Open

exam.q: 5. Explain one difference between a vulnerability assessment and a penetration test.
pts: A vulnerability assessment finds and lists weaknesses but does not try to break in
whereas a penetration test has an ethical hacker actively try to break in, with permission, to prove the impact
exam.tip: A difference needs both sides. Link with "whereas".

exam.sc: Meridian Print & Design is a medium-sized company. It has an office network of around 60 devices, a public-facing e-commerce website (online shop), Windows workstations and staff who have had very little security training, and no system to track problems once they have been found.
exam.q: 6(a). State one tool Meridian could use to assess its e-commerce website.
pts: Website vulnerability scanner

exam.sc: Meridian Print & Design is a medium-sized company. It has an office network of around 60 devices, a public-facing e-commerce website (online shop), Windows workstations and staff who have had very little security training, and no system to track problems once they have been found.
exam.q: 6(b). Explain why Meridian should use a network mapper on its office network.
pts: With around 60 devices, a mapper shows every device including rogue ones
so unknown devices can be removed and none are missed when patching
exam.tip: Use the "60 devices" from the scenario.

exam.sc: Meridian Print & Design is a medium-sized company. It has an office network of around 60 devices, a public-facing e-commerce website (online shop), Windows workstations and staff who have had very little security training, and no system to track problems once they have been found.
exam.q: 6(c). The assessment produces a long list of findings. Explain how the IT manager should decide which issues to deal with first.
pts: Use the CVSS score and deal with the highest first
because a high score means the most serious damage if exploited
Consider how exposed/easy to exploit it is, e.g. the public e-commerce site
so it is more likely to be attacked and holds customer payment data, so the impact is greatest
exam.tip: 4-mark explain = two points, each with a reason. Use the scenario.

exam.sc: Meridian Print & Design is a medium-sized company. It has an office network of around 60 devices, a public-facing e-commerce website (online shop), Windows workstations and staff who have had very little security training, and no system to track problems once they have been found.
exam.q: 6(d). Explain one advantage of using vulnerability detection and management software instead of a one-off scan.
pts: It scans regularly and tracks each fix until done
Meridian has no system to track problems, so issues won't be forgotten and new ones are caught
exam.tip: The scenario says "no system to track problems". Use it.

exam.sc: Meridian Print & Design is a medium-sized company. It has an office network of around 60 devices, a public-facing e-commerce website (online shop), Windows workstations and staff who have had very little security training, and no system to track problems once they have been found.
exam.q: 6(e). Explain one limitation of relying only on automated scanning tools.
pts: They can miss zero-day flaws or give false negatives
which gives a false sense of security, so an attacker could still get in
